symbols.name: T
symbols.def: A nonempty increment set disjoint from \(L\), with \(|T|\le k\).

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Uniform conditional residual-variance floor, denoted \(\sigma_{\min}^2\) in the motivating question.

symbols.name: Tcal
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak T=\{(p,k,m,M,s,V):p\in\mathbb N,\ p\ge2,\ 1\le k\le\lfloor p/2\rfloor,\ 0<m\le M,\ 0<s\le V\}\).

symbols.name: Mlin
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lin}}\) is the information model in Lin et al. (2025) in which the observed laws \(\mathcal L(X,Y_0)\) and \(\mathcal L(X,Y_1)\) share the pretreatment-covariate marginal.

symbols.name: Mpk
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\), the explicitly defined randomized Gaussian sparse-margin class for each \(p,k,m,M,s,V\) in \(\mathfrak T\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: Known envelope for the coordinates of the Gaussian mean vector used only for uniform inference.

symbols.name: Madm
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{adm}}_{p,k}(m,M,s,V;\pi_0,G)\), the inference subclass of \(\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\) with treatment overlap, bounded means, and \(\Sigma\succeq mI_p\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The sharp lower endpoint for \(\tau_2\) after retaining \(X_S\).

symbols.name: gamma_k
symbols.def: Budget-\(k\) submodularity ratio of \(F\), with zero denominators omitted and value one if all denominators vanish.

symbols.name: Shat
symbols.def: Empirical forward-greedy set built from \(\widehat B\).

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: Approximation tolerance for the extremal construction.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Unequal-scale perturbation in the extremal Gaussian family.

symbols.name: eps0
symbols.def: Control-arm residual noise in the extremal family.

symbols.name: eps1
symbols.def: Treatment-arm residual noise in the extremal family.

symbols.name: Ph
symbols.def: The joint probability law of \(A,X,Y_0,Y_1\) in the fully specified \(p=2k\) unequal-scale Gaussian construction indexed by \(h\).

symbols.name: Acal
symbols.def: Fixed candidate family from which selection is made.

symbols.name: dtheta
symbols.def: \(d_p=p(p+1)/2+3p+5\), the dimension of the Gaussian observed-data moment parameter.

symbols.name: Ptheta
symbols.def: \(P_{\vartheta}\) is the unique randomized Gaussian law of \(O\) whose moment parameter is \(\vartheta\in\Theta\).

symbols.name: btheta
symbols.def: \(b_S(\vartheta)\) is the closed-form Gaussian endpoint obtained by evaluating the formula for \(B(S)\) at \(\vartheta\).

symbols.name: psiS
symbols.def: \(\psi_S(O;\vartheta)\), the influence function of \(b_S(\vartheta)\) under the Gaussian moment map.

symbols.name: nuStar
symbols.def: Fixed positive influence-standard-deviation separation for ordinary Wald inference.

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: \(Z(O)=(A,X^{\mathsf T},\operatorname{vech}(XX^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T},I_0Y,I_1Y,(I_0XY)^{\mathsf T},(I_1XY)^{\mathsf T},I_0Y^2,I_1Y^2)^{\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: Bonferroni raw-moment confidence region represented as a random closed subset of \(\Theta\).

symbols.name: rho_k
symbols.def: \(\rho_k(K,R)=\inf\{\gamma_k(F):p\in\mathbb N,\ m,M,s,V>0,\ (p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T,\ M/m=K,\ V/s=R,\ P\in\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\}\).

symbols.name: Hfix
symbols.def: Feasible-frame reduction for the fixed-\(k\) frontier.

standard.name: Uniform nonsingularity of the finite-dimensional covariance parameter

assumptions.condition: \((X,Y_a)\) is jointly Gaussian for every \(a\in\mathcal I_2\).

novel.justification: This conditional-noise margin is satisfied by Gaussian linear outcome models whose arm-specific independent noise variances are at least \(s\); it permits heterogeneous observed scales and does not specify any subset gain or approximation ratio.

standard.name: Candidate-uniform influence-variance nondegeneracy at a moment parameter

definitions.name: Admissible dimension-and-margin tuples
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak T=\{(p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathbb N^2\times(0,\infty)^4:p\ge2,\ 1\le k\le\lfloor p/2\rfloor,\ m\le M,\ s\le V\}\).

definitions.name: Randomized Gaussian sparse-margin class
definitions.construction: For each \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\), \(\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)=\{P\text{ on }\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R^2:0<\pi<1,\ A\perp(X,Y_0,Y_1),\ (X,Y_a)\text{ is jointly Gaussian for every }a\in\mathcal I_2,\ \Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^p,\ mI_{|U|}\preceq\Sigma_{UU}\preceq MI_{|U|}\text{ for every }U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\text{ with }|U|\le2k,\ \min\{r_0(S),r_1(S)\}\ge s\text{ for every }S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\text{ with }|S|\le2k,\ \max\{v_0,v_1\}\le V\}\).

definitions.name: Budgeted submodularity ratio
definitions.construction: \(\gamma_k(F)=\min\!\left\{1,\inf_{\substack{L\cap T=\varnothing,\ |L|\le k,\ 1\le|T|\le k\\ \Delta(L,T)>0}}\frac{\sum_{j\in T}\Delta(L,\{j\})}{\Delta(L,T)}\right\}\), with value one when the infimum set is empty.

definitions.name: Residual-score lifts
definitions.construction: For disjoint \(L,T\), compute \(H\), \(d_0\), \(d_1\), \(u_0\), and \(u_1\) by their symbol-table formulas and lift each score by \(z(u)=(u^{\mathsf T},\sqrt{1-\|u\|_2^2})^{\mathsf T}\).

definitions.name: Population forward greedy
definitions.construction: Set \(S_0=\varnothing\) and recursively choose \(j_i\in\arg\max_{j\notin S_{i-1}}\{F(S_{i-1}\cup\{j\})-F(S_{i-1})\}\), then set \(S_g=S_k\).

definitions.name: Empirical forward greedy
definitions.construction: Apply \(\text{def:greedy}\) with \(\widehat F(S)=\widehat B(S)-\widehat B(\varnothing)\) and deterministic tie breaking to obtain \(\widehat S\).

definitions.name: Fully randomized unequal-scale radial family
definitions.construction: For \(p=2k\), draw \(X\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\) with \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}\{KI_k-(K-1)\mathbf 1_k\mathbf 1_k^{\mathsf T}/k,I_k\}\). Independently draw \(\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,1)\) and \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\). For \(0<h<R-1\), set \(Y_0=\sqrt{R-1}\,\mathbf 1_k^{\mathsf T}X_{1:k}/\sqrt{k}+\varepsilon_0\), \(Y_1=\sqrt{R-h-1}\,\mathbf 1_k^{\mathsf T}X_{1:k}/\sqrt{k}+\varepsilon_1\), and \(Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\). Define \(P_h\) as the resulting joint law of \(A,X,Y_0,Y_1\), whose observed datum is \(O=(A,X,Y)\).

definitions.name: Observed Gaussian moment and covariance maps
Evaluation-sample Gaussian endpoint estimator
definitions.construction: Estimate \(\theta(P_{\vartheta})\) on \(D_2\) by arm-specific sample means, variances, and outcome-covariances together with the pooled covariate covariance, and set \(\widehat B(S)=b_S(\widehat\vartheta)\).

definitions.name: Gaussian endpoint influence function
definitions.construction: For \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), \(\psi_S(O;\vartheta)=2(\mu_1-\mu_0)\{I_1e_1/\pi-I_0e_0/(1-\pi)\}+(1-t_S)I_0(e_0^2-v_0)/(1-\pi)+(1-t_S^{-1})I_1(e_1^2-v_1)/\pi+2\sqrt{t_S}\,w_S^{\mathsf T}I_0(x_Se_0-c_{0,S})/(1-\pi)-2w_S^{\mathsf T}I_1(x_Se_1-c_{1,S})/(\sqrt{t_S}\pi)-w_S^{\mathsf T}(x_Sx_S^{\mathsf T}-\Sigma_{SS})w_S\), where every component is evaluated at \(\vartheta\).

definitions.name: Selected endpoint Wald interval
definitions.construction:
\(I_S=[\widehat B(S)-z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat
u_S/\sqrt{n_2},\widehat B(S)+z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat
u_S/\sqrt{n_2}]\), where \(\widehat
u_S^2\) is the sample variance of the plug-in influence function \(\psi_S\) on \(D_2\).

definitions.name: Whole-class moment-projection interval
definitions.construction: Let \(\widehat q\) and \(\widehat\omega_j^2\) be the sample mean and coordinate variances of \(Z\) on \(D_2\), and set \(C=\{\vartheta\in\Theta:|Q_j(\vartheta)-\widehat q_j|\le z_{1-\alpha/(2d_p)}\widehat\omega_j/\sqrt{n_2}\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,d_p\}\). If \(C\ne\varnothing\), set \(J_S=[\inf_{\vartheta\in C}b_S(\vartheta),\sup_{\vartheta\in C}b_S(\vartheta)]\); if \(C=\varnothing\), set \(J_S=[\min_{\vartheta\in\Theta}b_S(\vartheta),\max_{\vartheta\in\Theta}b_S(\vartheta)]\).

definitions.name: Exact fixed-budget Gaussian frontier
definitions.construction: \(\rho_k(K,R)=\inf\{\gamma_k(F):p\in\mathbb N,\ m,M,s,V>0,\ (p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T,\ M/m=K,\ V/s=R,\ P\in\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\}\).

definitions.name: Feasible-frame handle for the exact fixed-budget frontier
definitions.construction: Reduce the search for \(\rho_k(K,R)\) to positive-definite Schur complements \(H\) with spectrum in \([m,M]\), their normalized coordinate frame, and pairs of feasible hemisphere scores \((u_0,u_1)\) satisfying the residual-radius constraints; optimize the exact sum of singleton angular losses relative to the joint angular loss without replacing either by a global Lipschitz envelope.

statements.statement: For every \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\), \(\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\subset\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lin}}\). The inclusion is strict because the published information model permits non-Gaussian arm marginals and imposes no sparse spectral or residual-floor margins.
statements.justification: The inclusion makes explicit that the budget frontier is a structured theorem inside the published conditional-transport information model rather than a redefined causal target.
statements.gap: Lin et al. (2025) work over a broader information class; sparse Gaussian margins are introduced here to obtain a quantitative selection frontier.
statements.consumer: Readers can distinguish which conclusions transfer to general conditional transport and which rely on the tractable Gaussian planning subclass.

statements.statement: For every \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\), every \(P\in\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\), and every \(|S|\le2k\), the sharp information-specific lower endpoint is \[B(S)=(\mu_1-\mu_0)^2+(c_{1,S}-c_{0,S})^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}(c_{1,S}-c_{0,S})+(\sqrt{r_1(S)}-\sqrt{r_0(S)})^2.\] It is attained by coupling the two conditional Gaussian residuals through one common standard normal.
statements.justification: This proposition makes the causal partial-identification endpoint explicit and supplies the algebraic object whose information increments can be compared.
statements.gap: Lin et al. (2025), Example 3.8 and Lemma 5.1, give Gaussian conditional-transport formulas in special models; the present formula covers arbitrary retained coordinate sets and records direct information-specific attainment.
statements.consumer: A trial planner can evaluate the sharp lower bound on mean squared individual effects from arm-specific first and second moments for any candidate baseline panel.

statements.statement: For disjoint \(L,T\) with \(|L|\le k\), \(1\le|T|\le k\), and \(|L\cup T|\le2k\), \[\Delta(L,T)=2\sqrt{r_0(L)r_1(L)}\,g(u_0,u_1)=\sqrt{r_0(L)r_1(L)}\,\|z(u_0)-z(u_1)\|_2^2.\] Moreover \(mI\preceq H\preceq MI\), \(H^{1/2}\operatorname{diag}(H)^{-1}H^{1/2}\succeq(m/M)I\), and \(\|u_a\|_2^2\le1-s/V\) for both arms.
statements.justification: The chordal identity isolates the exact two-arm geometry and the frame inequality retains coordinate meaning after residualization.
statements.gap: Neither the fixed-set Gaussian formulas of Lin et al. nor the regression spectral proof of Das and Kempe derives this coupled upper-hemisphere information identity.
statements.consumer: The identity turns a causal-bound selection problem into a geometric frame comparison that can be reused for certificates and diagnostics.

statements.statement: For every \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\), \(F\) is normalized, nonnegative, and monotone, and \[\gamma_k(F)\ge\Gamma=\frac{m}{M}\frac{s}{V}=\frac{1}{KR}.\] The bound is independent of \(p\) and \(k\).
statements.justification: This is the central achievability theorem: sparse covariance conditioning and residual signal-to-noise margins alone certify a nonvanishing approximation ratio.
statements.gap: Lin et al. leave variable selection open, while Das and Kempe control a one-response regression objective; neither supplies the extra residual-scale factor or the causal transport comparison.
statements.consumer: Investigators facing a hard baseline-measurement budget obtain an ex ante certificate for forward selection without dependence on the number of available covariates.

statements.statement: For every integer \(k\ge2\), every \(K\ge1\), every \(R>1\), and every \(\eta>0\), some sufficiently small \(h\in(0,R-1)\) makes the fully specified law \(P_h\), with \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independent of the Gaussian potential-outcome system and \(Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\), a member of \(\mathcal M_{2k,k}(1,K,1,R)\). Its arm variances and its conditional scales on every proper active subset are unequal, and \[\gamma_k(F;P_h)\le\frac{k}{1+(k-1)KR}+\eta.\] Consequently, both \(K\) and \(R\) are necessary factors, and \(1/(KR)\) is the largest lower certificate depending only on \((K,R)\) that holds uniformly over dimensions and budgets.
statements.justification: The realizable unequal-scale family certifies that neither condition factor is a proof artifact and closes the dimension-free minimax comparison.
statements.gap: Bian et al. construct abstract tight set functions, but do not show that such bad geometry is realizable by a legal Gaussian causal conditional-transport model.
statements.consumer: Method developers learn exactly which covariance and residual margins must improve to obtain a stronger dimension-free selection guarantee.

statements.statement: Population forward greedy satisfies \[F(S_g)\ge\left\{1-\left(1-\frac{\Gamma}{k}\right)^k\right\}\mathrm{OPT}\ge(1-e^{-\Gamma})\mathrm{OPT}.\] On the event \(\max_{|S|\le k}|\widehat B(S)-B(S)|\le\epsilon\), empirical forward greedy satisfies \[F(\widehat S)\ge\left\{1-\left(1-\frac{\Gamma}{k}\right)^k\right\}\mathrm{OPT}-4k\epsilon.\]
statements.justification: This theorem translates the model-specific frontier into the performance guarantee needed by a budget-constrained analyst.
statements.gap: The recurrence is generic machinery from Das--Kempe and Bian et al.; the new input is the sharp causal Gaussian certificate supplied by the preceding theorems.
statements.consumer: A baseline-panel designer obtains both a population approximation factor and a finite estimation-error tolerance for the chosen panel.

statements.statement: Fix \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\), \(\pi_0\in(0,1/2)\), and \(G<\infty\). The image \(\Theta=\{\theta(P):P\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{adm}}_{p,k}(m,M,s,V;\pi_0,G)\}\) is compact. For each fixed \(\nu_*>0\), the Wald-separated image \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\) is a compact subset of \(\Theta\). The raw-moment map \(Q:\Theta\to Q(\Theta)\) is continuous and one-to-one with continuous inverse, every \(b_S\) with \(S\in\mathcal A\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\Theta\), and \(\Omega:\Theta\to\mathbb S_+^{d_p}\) is continuous with \(\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\min_{1\le j\le d_p}\Omega_{jj}(\vartheta)>0\).
statements.justification: This proposition puts compactness, endpoint smoothness, and raw-moment covariance regularity in the finite-dimensional parameter space on which both inference procedures operate.
statements.gap: These are standard finite-dimensional Gaussian moment facts used to specialize generic sample-split and projection inference; they are not part of the angular-frontier novelty claim.
statements.consumer: The two inference theorems obtain a type-correct common domain and well-defined uniformity quantifiers.

For every \(\vartheta\in\Theta\) and \(S\in\mathcal A\), \(
u_S^2(\vartheta)=0\) if and only if \(b_S(\vartheta)=0\), equivalently \(\mu_0=\mu_1\), \(\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}c_{0,S}=\Sigma_{SS}^{-1}c_{1,S}\), and \(r_0(S)=r_1(S)\). Hence every equality parameter is excluded from \(\Theta_+(
u_*)\) for every fixed \(
u_*>0\).
statements.justification: The equivalence isolates the quadratic equality boundary and makes the domains of ordinary Wald and projection inference disjoint where first-order studentization fails.
statements.gap: Lin et al. identify equality as a degeneracy point for a fixed quadratic transport target; this proposition records the exact Gaussian selected-endpoint criterion needed to route inference, without claiming a new generic selection principle.
statements.consumer: Analysts can determine from the moment parameter whether to use separated Wald inference or the whole-image projection interval.

statements.justification: The theorem gives exact conditional post-selection coverage uniformly on the explicitly separated moment subclass where every candidate endpoint has nonzero first-order variance.
statements.gap: Ji--Lei--Spector already provide generic selection-valid inference, and Lin et al. provide a fixed-target quadratic-COT central limit theorem; this Gaussian specialization supplies the endpoint influence map and its exact degeneracy criterion, not a new generic selection principle.
statements.consumer: Analysts can report uncertainty for the held-out endpoint selected by any first-sample budget rule on \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\).

statements.statement: For every \(D_1\)-measurable \(\widehat S\in\mathcal A\), the moment-projection interval obeys \[\liminf_{n_2\to\infty}\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{D_1}P_{\vartheta}\{b_{\widehat S}(\vartheta)\in J_{\widehat S}\mid D_1\}\ge1-\alpha.\] This whole-image claim includes every equality parameter \(\vartheta\in\Theta\) satisfying \(b_{\widehat S}(\vartheta)=0\), for which \(\nu_{\widehat S}^2(\vartheta)=0\) and ordinary Wald inference is unavailable.
statements.justification: Projection restores honest coverage exactly on the equality boundary where first-order studentization degenerates.
statements.gap: Imbens--Manski and Stoye address collapsing estimated bounds under regular Gaussian endpoint limits; the proposed interval instead projects primitive Gaussian moments and remains valid when the selected endpoint has zero first derivative.
statements.consumer: Empirical users obtain a conservative fallback that covers the selected causal lower endpoint over the entire compact moment image \(\Theta\).

statements.statement: Using the feasible-frame handle \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{fix}}\), determine the exact value of \(\rho_k(K,R)\) for each fixed \(k\ge2\), where the infimum ranges over every \(p,m,M,s,V\) satisfying \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\), \(M/m=K\), and \(V/s=R\), and every \(P\in\mathcal M_{p,k}(m,M,s,V)\). In particular, establish whether every such Gaussian objective satisfies \(\gamma_k(F)\ge k/[1+(k-1)KR]\), or construct a member of this class violating the inequality and derive the corrected fixed-budget frontier.
statements.justification: The dimension-free frontier is closed, but exact finite-budget geometry may yield a materially stronger certificate for the small budgets used in practice.
statements.gap: The constructed family attains the rational expression in the vanishing-contrast limit, while neither generic weak-submodularity theory nor the current angular comparison proves it is universal.
statements.consumer: A fixed-budget trial planner would replace the asymptotic dimension-free certificate by the best possible finite-\(k\) guarantee.

sampling_model.design: Randomized binary treatment with known allocation probability \(\pi\in[\pi_0,1-\pi_0]\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of \(O=(A,X,Y)\) from the observed Gaussian law \(P_{\vartheta}\) indexed by \(\vartheta\in\Theta\); ordinary Wald inference is restricted to \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\), while projection inference and the angular frontier retain their stated whole-class domains.
sampling_model.overlap: The allocation probability is uniformly separated from zero and one.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite-dimensional map \(\theta(P)\) is estimated from arm-specific means, variances, and outcome-covariances and the pooled covariate covariance on an evaluation split independent of covariate selection.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Covariates monotonically tighten conditional-transport partial-identification bounds and variable selection is left as a future direction.
Sparse covariance eigenvalues lower-bound the regression submodularity ratio and yield a forward-selection approximation guarantee.
Submodularity ratio and generalized curvature jointly yield a tight generic cardinality-constrained greedy guarantee.
Multiplier-bootstrap aggregation permits valid covariate and model selection among conditional-transport dual bounds.
A smooth-density quadratic conditional-transport estimator has a fixed-target central limit theorem away from equality.
A short never-empty confidence interval is valid when estimated lower and upper bounds have a regular joint Gaussian limit.

tldr: For a randomized Gaussian experiment, retaining a subset of pretreatment covariates raises the sharp conditional-optimal-transport lower endpoint for the mean squared individual treatment effect. Each endpoint increment equals a squared chordal distance between upper-hemisphere lifts of two residualized arm-score vectors. A sparse Schur-complement frame bound and a hemisphere Lipschitz comparison imply \(\gamma_k\ge(m/M)(s/V)\), so forward greedy attains a dimension-free fraction of the best size-\(k\) tightening. A fully specified randomized unequal-scale observed-data family approaches \(k/[1+(k-1)(M/m)(V/s)]\), proving that both margin factors are necessary and that the dimension-free certificate is optimal as the budget varies. On the compact image \(\Theta\), independent evaluation yields credited conditional Wald inference on the separated subclass \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\) and a conservative raw-moment projection interval over all of \(\Theta\), including equality. The exact fixed-\(k\) frontier remains an explicit open problem.

project_justification.gap: Conditional optimal transport supplies sharp covariate-assisted causal bounds, but existing work treats the conditioning set as fixed. Generic weak-submodularity theory does not determine the approximation ratio of the unequal-scale two-arm Gaussian endpoint.
project_justification.niche: The Gaussian endpoint has a residual-score geometry that is absent from one-response regression: singleton and joint gains are chordal distances observed through a sparse Schur-complement frame.
project_justification.fill: The project derives that geometry, proves the optimal dimension-free margin certificate with a fully randomized unequal-scale lower family, transfers it to greedy selection, and formulates credited sample-split Wald inference on \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\) together with projection inference on the full compact moment image \(\Theta\).

related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2025) motivate covariate-assisted conditional transport, prove interpolation toward the conditional bound, give Gaussian benchmarks, and identify variable selection as future work. Their AISTATS paper (2026) establishes sharp fixed-information bounds and adapted-Wasserstein estimation, while their smooth-density paper (2026) gives rates and a fixed-target quadratic central limit theorem. Das and Kempe (2011) introduce the submodularity ratio and its sparse-spectral control for regression; Bian et al. (2017) and Elenberg et al. (2018) provide generic greedy and restricted-curvature machinery. Ji, Lei, and Spector (2023) already establish selection-valid inference among covariate and model choices, so that principle is not positioned as new. Gelbrich (1990) and Fang and Zhu (2020) explain why covariance transport geometry extends to some elliptical laws but not automatically through conditioning. Imbens and Manski (2004) and Stoye (2021) motivate honest inference at delicate partial-identification boundaries; the present projection interval uses their lesson without claiming a new length-optimal procedure.
technical_internal_limitation: The sharpness family has a positive but vanishing endpoint contrast as \(h\downarrow0\), which is legitimate for a ratio frontier but does not establish a worst-case greedy-value ratio at a fixed signal amplitude. Ordinary Wald inference is asserted only on \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\); equality laws satisfy \(b_S=0\) and \(\nu_S^2=0\) and are handled by whole-image projection. Computing the best sparse margins may itself be combinatorial, so the theorem accepts certified values of \(m,M,s,V\) as inputs.
honest_scope: The dimension-free certificate, its two-factor necessity, and the greedy consequence are theorem targets over the explicitly quantified Gaussian law classes. The extremal construction specifies the covariate law, independent arm noises, independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment, potential outcomes, and observed outcome. Sample-split Wald coverage on \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\) and conservative projection coverage on all of \(\Theta\), including equality laws, are credited finite-dimensional inference specializations rather than novelty claims. The exact fixed-\(k\) lower frontier and any locally shortest equality-boundary interval remain open. When \(k=1\), every positive submodularity ratio equals one and greedy is optimal. On the equal-scale slice \(v_0=v_1\) and \(c_1=-c_0\), the gain reduces to the classical regression explained-variance objective, recovering the known sparse-spectral setting. When \(R=1\), all covariate-outcome covariances vanish and \(F\equiv0\), so the ratio convention returns one.

seed_details.question: Over randomized unequal-scale Gaussian arm laws, characterize the largest dimension-free lower bound on the submodularity ratio of the size-\(k\) conditional-transport gain from sparse covariance conditioning and residual-variance margins alone.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Lin et al. establish that covariates tighten conditional-transport bounds and explicitly suggest forward selection, but their first missing step is a comparison between joint and coordinate endpoint increments under a cardinality budget.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace their fixed-conditioning Gaussian transport calculation by a Schur-complement residualization, then compare singleton and joint increments through upper-hemisphere lifts.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches joining conditional optimal transport with covariate selection, cardinality budgets, submodularity ratios, and greedy approximation found generic selection machinery but no causal conditional-transport frontier.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Uses the native transport representation and a generic-class sharpness family; the inference rung is secondary and is not labeled as a standalone motif.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Das and Kempe because their sparse-eigenvalue argument already lower-bounds every covariance-driven subset objective.
seed_details.rebuttal: The unequal-scale endpoint contains coupled square-root residual terms and is not the regression \(R^2\) objective; the first non-generic step is the exact angular identity, and the matching unequal-scale family proves dependence on a second, causal residual-scale factor.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Definition 2.3, Lemma 2.4 and its spectral proof, Theorem 3.2 and its greedy proof, Section 6.1, and the conclusion of the arXiv source.
seed_details.question: Is \(k/[1+(k-1)KR]\) the exact worst-case submodularity ratio at every fixed budget \(k\) for the unequal-scale Gaussian conditional-transport gain?
seed_details.proof_boundary: The sparse-eigenvalue proof of Das and Kempe controls regression explained variance, while fixed-budget sharpness here requires solving the coupled two-arm hemispherical Gram problem rather than applying the generic spectral inequality.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After residualization, retain the exact hemisphere metric instead of replacing it by its global Lipschitz envelope, and optimize the coordinate frame under Schur-complement feasibility.
seed_details.destination_search: The target-method search for fixed-cardinality weak-submodularity constants under Gaussian conditional transport found no occupied result; Bian et al. optimize over abstract set functions, not realizable Gaussian transport objectives.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed asks for a uniform fixed-budget frontier over a nondegenerate law class, not a witness at one hand-tuned law.
seed_details.red_team: The proposed rational expression is merely the value of one equicorrelated construction and has no reason to be universal.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection is presently unresolved rather than dispositive; the seed is retained only as an explicit open-ended question with a feasible-frame handle, not asserted as a theorem.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorem 1, the linear-program proof in Section 3, the tightness construction, and the conclusion of the arXiv source.
seed_details.question: Does Gaussian conditional-transport geometry force a nontrivial generalized-curvature upper bound that strictly improves the greedy factor beyond the submodularity-ratio guarantee?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Bian et al. give a tight abstract \((\gamma,\alpha)\) guarantee, but do not characterize curvature for a realizable two-arm conditional-transport set function.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Bound reverse marginal losses using the same residual-score lifts while tracking how the Schur complement changes after conditioning on a larger set.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for curvature bounds for Wasserstein or conditional-transport feature selection found no result specialized to the Gaussian endpoint.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Curvature is the focal structural parameter; the seed is not forced into an unrelated partial-identification representation motif.
seed_details.red_team: This is generic Bian et al. once any curvature number is inserted.
seed_details.rebuttal: The missing theorem would have to derive curvature from observable covariance and residual margins; nevertheless, no feasible nontrivial bound emerged from the anchor geometry, so it is not used in the core.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Definition 3.1, Proposition 3.3, Theorem 3.4, Proposition 3.5, Theorem 3.6 and its proof architecture, and Section 5 of the arXiv source.
seed_details.question: Can a data-driven size choice minimize mean squared endpoint error by balancing monotone population tightening against the covariate-dimensional wavelet bias and variance?
seed_details.proof_boundary: The published wavelet expansion fixes the conditioning dimension; selecting a subset changes both the target functional and the smoothing resolution before the stability remainder is controlled.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Uniformize the quadratic stability expansion over a nested collection of conditioning sets and combine it with a penalized estimate of omitted tightening.
seed_details.destination_search: The target-method pair of wavelet conditional transport and oracle cardinality selection is not covered by Lin et al. or by Ji et al.'s validity-oriented model comparison.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The named object is an endpoint-risk frontier, so the seed uses M11 rather than treating M8 as a standalone shape.
seed_details.red_team: This is routine structural-risk minimization with the rate table of Lin et al. plugged into a penalty.
seed_details.rebuttal: A valid rebuttal would require a uniform cross-target expansion and an estimable tightening bias, neither supplied by the fixed-target paper; the construction remains materially less mature than the angular frontier.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Section 2.3 on multiplier selection, Corollary 2.1 and its proof architecture, the continuous-outcome variance-of-treatment-effect example, Appendix C on cross-fitted model selection, and the discussion of the current arXiv source.
seed_details.question: What is the local minimax expected-length frontier for confidence intervals for a greedy-selected Gaussian endpoint when the residual-score lifts coincide?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Ji et al.'s multiplier method controls selection among valid dual bounds, but its nondegeneracy conditions do not resolve the zero-derivative quadratic boundary where both the endpoint and its first-order variance vanish.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive the local quadratic Gaussian experiment for residual-score differences before calibrating a whole-class interval, rather than studentizing a first-order dual score.
seed_details.destination_search: Stoye and Imbens--Manski treat collapsing or misspecified bound intervals; Lin et al. note faster-than-root-\(n\) behavior at equality, but none studies selected Gaussian conditional-transport endpoint length optimality.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is a local limit and expected-length frontier uniform through a quadratic boundary, not generic post-selection coverage.
seed_details.red_team: Generic projection or moment-selection inference already gives uniform coverage.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coverage is settled, but optimal expected length in the selected quadratic local experiment is not; the present core therefore uses only conservative projection and does not claim this seed's stronger result.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, the Gelbrich inequality lemma, Theorems 1 and 2 with their covariance-generator constructions, and the conclusion of the arXiv source.
seed_details.question: For conditionally elliptical arms, identify whether a common radial generator yields a positive dimension-free covariate-budget frontier and, if so, its generator-dependent constant.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Fang and Zhu show covariance-based Wasserstein identities for elliptical families, but conditioning on a subset can change the radial generator, so the Gaussian conditional angular identity is the first step that fails.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Characterize the conditional radial law after Schur complementation and determine whether its transport increment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the Gaussian chordal metric.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches joining conditional elliptical transport, sparse covariate selection, and weak submodularity found no destination paper.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The elliptical coupling geometry is non-LP and the claim ranges over a generator-indexed class rather than one engineered distribution.
seed_details.red_team: Gelbrich's formula transfers the Gaussian proof verbatim to common-generator elliptical laws.
seed_details.rebuttal: The common-generator property is generally not preserved uniformly across conditioning values and subsets, so unconditional equality does not supply the required increment identity.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Proposition 2.2, Theorems 3.1--3.2 and their adapted-Wasserstein proof steps, Theorems 4.1--4.3, and Section 6 of the arXiv source.
seed_details.question: How well can a Gaussian covariance surrogate select covariates for the true non-elliptical quadratic conditional-transport gain under explicit distributional shape restrictions?
seed_details.proof_boundary: The direct adapted-Wasserstein estimator targets true conditional transport, whereas a covariance surrogate only lower-bounds each fixed transport cost and does not compare marginal gains across subsets.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Decompose every subset gain into the Gelbrich component and a non-ellipticity slack, then control differences of that slack across nested conditioning sets.
seed_details.destination_search: No approximation theorem connecting Gelbrich-surrogate subset selection to true conditional-transport subset selection was found.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed seeks a transport-slack sandwich or a class-wide impossibility result, avoiding an LP reformulation of a coupling problem.
seed_details.red_team: Gelbrich's inequality directly implies the surrogate-selected set approximates the true optimum.
seed_details.rebuttal: Pointwise lower bounds do not order incremental gains; without a shape condition, moment-matched laws can alter transport slack while leaving the selector unchanged.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Definition 2, Theorem 1, the least-favorable calibration proof, and the conclusion of the arXiv source.
seed_details.question: Can a short never-empty interval adapt simultaneously to a zero endpoint, a switching greedy path, and unequal Gaussian arm scales?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Stoye's interval starts from asymptotically normal lower and upper bounds, while a selected squared-distance endpoint has a degenerate first derivative at equality and a nonsmooth maximum over paths.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the Gaussian first-order bound experiment by a projected quadratic-moment experiment indexed by candidate greedy paths.
seed_details.destination_search: The selected quadratic-boundary target is not covered by the never-empty interval or current conditional-transport inference papers.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposed contribution is a selected-boundary limit and length result; conservative projection alone is explicitly not presented as the kernel.
seed_details.red_team: A Bonferroni interval over all subsets already solves the problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: It solves honesty but not the proposed length adaptation; because the length theorem is not yet tractable, only the conservative projection component is retained in the chosen core.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorem 4.3 and its stability proof, Section 5.3, and the variable-selection paragraph of Section 6 of the arXiv source.
seed_details.question: Can sequentially purchased baseline covariates be stopped at a data-adaptive budget while retaining an oracle guarantee for endpoint tightening net of measurement cost?
seed_details.proof_boundary: The fixed-budget gain comparison does not account for optional stopping or a random feasible family determined by earlier measurements.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Embed marginal transport gains in a filtration and derive a confidence sequence for net gain before optimizing a stopping rule.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for sequential covariate acquisition combined with causal conditional-transport bounds found active feature-acquisition work but no theorem for this partial-identification endpoint.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The decision variable is a sequential acquisition and stopping rule evaluated by net causal-bound value, rather than estimation error for a fixed endpoint.
seed_details.red_team: This is ordinary cost-sensitive feature acquisition with a new objective.
seed_details.rebuttal: The causal endpoint and partial-identification target are distinctive, but no theorem-level structural gain beyond generic acquisition machinery was identified, so the seed is dropped.

literature_map.settled: Conditional transport gives sharp information-specific bounds; fixed-conditioning Gaussian formulas, direct adapted-Wasserstein estimation, smooth-density rates, and a quadratic fixed-target central limit theorem are available.
literature_map.open_boundary: No inspected result gives a cardinality-constrained approximation ratio, a sparse-margin certificate, or a matching legal family for covariate selection.

literature_map.settled: Submodularity ratios, sparse-eigenvalue lower bounds for regression, generic greedy recurrences, curvature refinements, and abstract tight set functions are established.
literature_map.open_boundary: Those results do not derive the submodularity ratio or curvature of the unequal-scale Gaussian conditional-transport endpoint and do not certify realizability of their extremizers by causal Gaussian laws.

literature_map.settled: Sample splitting, multiplier selection among dual bounds, uniform inference for collapsing identified intervals, and never-empty intervals are established tools.
literature_map.open_boundary: Selection validity is not novel here; the remaining boundary-specific opportunity is a length-optimal quadratic local experiment, which this version does not claim.

literature_map.settled: The Gelbrich covariance expression is a universal quadratic-transport lower bound and is exact for structured elliptical families.
literature_map.open_boundary: Conditional subset selection can change the radial generator and the non-ellipticity slack, so no inspected theorem transfers the Gaussian budget frontier.
